title: Label Consensus
hints: How many labels can possibly have strictly more than half of the votes?
If you cross out two annotators who disagree, does a majority label stay a majority among the rest?

Keep a candidate and a counter: take a new candidate when the counter hits zero, add one on a match, subtract one otherwise. Then count the survivor in a second pass and print -1 unless it has more than half.

wrong.mode_only.cpp: prints the most common label even when it is only a plurality
wrong.no_confirm.cpp: trusts the Boyer-Moore survivor without a confirming second pass
wrong.tle_count_each.cpp: counts each label against all others in O(n^2) (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: up to 2*10^5 annotator labels, print the label with strictly more than half the votes or -1. Which plan fits?
options: Sort and print the middle label
Count labels in a hash map, or cancel disagreeing pairs with a candidate/counter and confirm in a second pass
Count each label by scanning the array once per label
strategy.why: The middle of a sorted array is the majority label if one exists, but it is not guaranteed to be one, and sorting costs O(n log n) without a check. Counting each label against the array is O(n^2). The most frequent label is only a plurality. A hash map or the candidate/counter vote with a confirming pass is O(n), and the vote needs only O(1) space.
